[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Introduction to Sharding in MongoDB"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Sharding is a method for distributing data across multiple machines. MongoDB uses sharding to support deployments with very large datasets and high throughput operations. Without sharding, the database's ability to scale is limited by the capacity of a single server."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Why Use Sharding?"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Horizontal Scaling: Sharding allows you to scale horizontally by adding more machines to your cluster."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Increased Throughput: Distributing data across multiple servers allows for parallel processing, increasing read and write throughput."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"High Availability: Sharding can improve availability by distributing data across multiple servers. If one shard goes down, the other shards can continue to serve data."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Sharding Components"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"A sharded MongoDB cluster consists of the following components:"},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Shard: Each shard contains a subset of the sharded data. In a production environment, each shard is a replica set."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Mongos: The mongos instances act as query routers, routing queries to the appropriate shards and aggregating the results. Clients connect to the mongos instances, not directly to the shards."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Config Servers: Config servers store metadata about the cluster, including the mapping of data chunks to shards. MongoDB uses config servers to manage the sharded cluster."},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Sharding Key"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"The sharding key determines how data is distributed across the shards. The choice of sharding key is critical to the performance of the sharded cluster. A good sharding key should:"},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Have high cardinality (many distinct values)."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Distribute writes evenly across the shards."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Support common query patterns."},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"MongoDB supports two types of sharding keys: ranged sharding and hashed sharding."},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"Ranged Sharding"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"With ranged sharding, data is divided into ranges based on the sharding key. Each range is assigned to a shard. Ranged sharding is suitable for applications where queries often target a specific range of values."},{"order":20,"type":"subheading","text":"Hashed Sharding"},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"With hashed sharding, the sharding key is hashed, and the hash value is used to determine the shard. Hashed sharding provides a more even distribution of data across the shards, but it is not suitable for range queries."},{"order":22,"type":"subheading","text":"Enabling Sharding"},{"order":23,"type":"paragraph","text":"To enable sharding for a database and collection, use the 'sh.enableSharding()' and 'sh.shardCollection()' methods in the 'mongo' shell."},{"order":24,"type":"code","text":"// Enable sharding for the 'mydatabase' database
sh.enableSharding("mydatabase")

// Shard the 'mycollection' collection using the 'key' field as the sharding key
sh.shardCollection("mydatabase.mycollection", { "key": "hashed" } )"},{"order":25,"type":"paragraph","text":"In the example above, the 'sh.enableSharding()' command enables sharding for the database named 'mydatabase'. The 'sh.shardCollection()' command shards the collection named 'mycollection' inside 'mydatabase', using the field 'key' as the sharding key. The 'hashed' value specifies that hashed sharding should be used."},{"order":26,"type":"subheading","text":"Considerations"},{"order":27,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Sharding adds complexity to your MongoDB deployment. It is important to carefully plan your sharding strategy before enabling sharding."},{"order":28,"type":"bullet_point","text":"The choice of sharding key is critical to the performance of the sharded cluster. Choose a sharding key that distributes data evenly across the shards and supports common query patterns."},{"order":29,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Monitor your sharded cluster closely to ensure that it is performing as expected."}]
